title: Explosives in Cyberspace
description: Compute decompressed lengths of a custom marker-based compression format.
writeup:
## Approach

The input is a compressed string using markers of the form (AxB), meaning: take the next A characters and repeat them B times. Whitespace is ignored. The challenge is that Part 1 and Part 2 interpret markers differently.

Part 1 treats markers non-recursively: the repeated block is copied as-is, without looking for markers inside it. Part 2 requires recursively computing the decompressed length of the repeated block, meaning nested markers must be expanded conceptually.

Because the fully decompressed string can be astronomically large, Part 2 must compute lengths mathematically rather than building the actual string.

## Part 1

We scan the string left to right. When we encounter a marker (AxB), we read the next A characters and append them B times to the output. Markers inside that block are treated as literal text. The final answer is simply the length of the decompressed output.

## Part 2

We compute the decompressed length using recursion. When encountering a marker (AxB), we recursively compute the decompressed length of the next A characters, then multiply that length by B. This allows nested markers to expand correctly without ever constructing the full string.

The final answer is the total decompressed length under recursive rules.
